plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional vector field plot drawn inside a light blue wireframe cube, with black x, y, and z axes running through it; x points toward the lower left, y to the right, and z vertically. A small shaded blue sphere sits where the axes cross, marked with the label 0, standing for a large mass at the origin. Arrows fill the interior of the cube and every one points inward toward that sphere. Those closest to the origin are long and bright orange, those at intermediate distance shorter and teal, and those near the corners and faces reduced to small dashes, so length and color together carry the magnitude of the field. Several of the longest arrows lie along the axis directions and meet the sphere head on. Because length and direction vary independently, the reader takes in both at once: the field aims at the central mass everywhere, and its strength climbs sharply as distance to the origin shrinks. The plot renders the gravitational field of a point mass, making visible the uniformly attractive radial direction and the rapid growth in magnitude near the source.

demo_steps.title: Direction toward the mass
demo_steps.narration: In direction-only mode, every arrow has the same length and points toward the blue sphere at the origin. The field is attractive everywhere and radial from all sides of the cube.

demo_steps.title: Add magnitude
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the magnitude-colored view. Arrows near the origin become longer and warmer in color, while arrows far from the mass shrink to small blue dashes.

demo_steps.title: Move closer to the origin
demo_steps.narration: Decrease r for the highlighted sample point. Its vector keeps pointing inward, but its length and color change sharply, showing the rapid increase in gravitational field strength near the mass.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: cube is 4 units on a side, centered at the origin, spanning x,y,z ∈ [-2,2]. Coordinate orientation should match the source: +z appears vertical upward, +y projects toward the right side of the page, and +x projects toward the lower-left; the negative halves of each axis pass through the cube in the opposite directions. Axes extend slightly outside the cube to about ±2.6 units and are black #111111 with arrowheads. Cube edges are thin light blue #48a9ff with no filled faces, or extremely transparent blue faces at opacity ≤0.04 if needed for depth. Origin sphere radius about 0.22 units, shaded pale blue #8fc7df with darker blue rim/shadow. Origin label '0' is black and sits just below/right of the sphere in screen space. Vector field samples should use a regular lattice such as coordinates {-1.6,-0.8,0,0.8,1.6} in each dimension, omitting points with r < 0.35 so arrows do not start inside the sphere. Field formula: for position vector p=(x,y,z), use F(p) = -k p / |p|^3, so direction is always toward the origin and magnitude is k/|p|^2; choose k=1 for normalization and clamp displayed arrow length to roughly 0.10–0.65 units. In magnitude-colored mode, map small magnitudes to dark blue #1f5aa6, intermediate magnitudes to teal #009688, high magnitudes to orange #f26c21, and highest near-origin arrows to red-orange #d93b2b. In direction-only mode, all arrows should be equal length around 0.22 units and a uniform blue/teal color. Highlighted sample point should lie on a fixed visible radial ray, for example direction normalize(0.85,0.35,0.35), so it appears to the right/front/up of the origin in the default view; its radius is controlled by the slider from 0.45 to 2.2. The highlighted sample arrow is thicker than the field arrows and points from the sample location toward the origin.
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.ArrowHelper or custom cylinder-plus-cone arrows; center each vector arrow at its lattice sample point with the arrowhead on the inward side. Recompute arrow length and color whenever sampleRadius or fieldMode changes. Keep the origin sphere rendered on top enough to remain visible, but allow nearby arrows to terminate just outside the sphere radius. Add simple Lambert/Phong lighting to make the central sphere visibly shaded like the source figure. Orbit should preserve the labeled axis directions and keep labels billboarding toward the camera.

action_items: Remove or hide the yellow sample point, dashed radial guide, highlighted sample arrow, and r label by default if aiming to match the source figure exactly.
